newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strategie Grains ups EU '97 grain crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: Strategie Grains ups EU '97 grain crop forecast.

text.p: French grain analyst Strategie Grains said on Monday it had revised upwards its forecast for the 1997 European Union grain crop to 201.1 million tonnes from last month's target of 199.8 million. This would mean a decline of one percent from 203.3 million tonnes produced in 1996.
In its August report, the analyst linked the revision to upwards adjustments in its forecasts for the barley and maize crops.
It predicted a 1997 barley crop of 51.9 million tonnes against 51.1 million last month and 51.7 million last in 1996.
The maize crop was forecast at 34.5 million tonnes against 34.1 million last month and so might exceed the 34.3 million produced in 1996, helped by benefitial rain in July and August.
Strategie Grains put the 1997 soft wheat crop at 89.1 million tonnes against 89 million last month and 90.9 million in 1996.
The new estimate assumes an average grain yield of 5.3 tonnes per hectare, unchanged from last month but down from 5.5 tonnes last year.
The analyst linked the stronger than expected barley crop to a four percent rise in area that offset a three percent decline in yields.
The maize yield was revised up to 8.3 tonnes from 8.2 tonnes last month and could thus be unchanged from last year while area could rise one percent.
The soft wheat yield was put at 6.4 tonnes per hectare, unchanged from last month and down three percent from last year.

June-July rain sparked unwanted wheat germination in the south of the European Union, including southern France. In the north there was concern over low specific weights but Hagberg numbers and protein content, two other key measurements of wheat quality, were satisfactory.
"It already appears that the quantity of wheat unfit for milling and for intervention (sale) will be substantial," the analyst warned.

Initial results showed satisfactory grain size and protein content for barley with the exception of Spain. Elsewhere there was some pre-germination problems for malting barley in Austria and in parts of France.
But because spring barley production remains strong, the EU will have more than enough malting barley to meet demand, the analyst said.
